note: Wednesday 07:00 SGT re-verify (pre-Asia-open) against the Tue 21 Jul US close. Tuesday snapped a three-day losing streak: S&P +0.89% to 7,509.20, Nasdaq +1.29% to 25,837.21, Dow +0.74% to 52,224.64, led by a memory-chip surge (Micron +12%, Sandisk +14%, AMD +8%); silver +~4% to ~$59, gold +~1.3-1.75% to ~$4,066-4,083, BTC to a five-week high ~$66.5k, 10-yr ~4.63%, Brent ~$89-90 on the US-Iran war. Fear&Greed is fetched LIVE in-browser with the baked value as fallback; breadth & regional flows are researched daily (no free real-time API). CNN's component-level API again returned an error this run, so the 7 sub-readings are inferred from sourced internals and labeled as such.

components.name: Market Momentum
components.reading: S&P 500 vs its 125-day moving average. The index rebounded +0.89% to ~7,509 on Tuesday 21 July, snapping a three-day losing streak and climbing back above its 50-DMA, roughly ~1% below its 2 June record and comfortably above a rising 200-DMA. Momentum improved from fear toward neutral as semis led the tape higher (Micron +12%, Sandisk +14%). [Inferred — CNN component API blocked this run]

components.name: Stock Price Strength
components.reading: Net 52-week highs vs lows on the NYSE. The Tuesday rally lifted new highs as the chip complex reversed higher; the net-highs read recovered from Monday's negative print toward balanced as energy/financials/semis all participated. Still short of the prior week's broadening. [Inferred from Barchart/exchange data]

components.name: Stock Price Breadth
components.reading: McClellan Volume Summation (advancing vs declining volume). The NYSE McClellan Oscillator ticked back positive on Tuesday's up-day after a near-zero, low-energy stretch; the Summation/RASI remains at a divergent lower high (~+366, below the +471 May peak), so participation is firming but not yet confirming a fresh thrust. [Inferred — mcoscillator]

components.name: Put/Call Options
components.reading: 5-day put/call ratio. Options demand eased off Monday's defensive tilt as equities rebounded and the semis complex reversed higher, though the active US-Iran war kept some hedging bid — a neutral-to-slightly-fearful read. [Inferred — CNN component API blocked]

components.name: Market Volatility
components.reading: VIX vs its 50-day moving average. The VIX eased back toward ~17 on Tuesday's risk-on session after Monday's ~18.8 spike, slipping back toward its 50-day average — a calming, neutral read. [Inferred]

components.name: Safe-Haven Demand
components.reading: 20-day stock vs Treasury bond return spread. Equities outperformed bonds sharply on Tuesday (10-yr yield up ~3bp to ~4.63% as stocks rallied), nudging this component back toward neutral from Monday's fear. [Inferred]

components.name: Junk Bond Demand
components.reading: Yield spread between junk bonds and investment-grade. HY OAS remains historically tight (~260-268bp) and firmed with the equity rally — credit continues to signal no stress, the most constructive component. [Inferred — FRED BAMLH0A0HYM2]

breadth.note: Breadth firmed with Tuesday's risk-on rebound: ~68.6% of S&P members are back above their 200-DMA (highest since February), the semis-led advance repaired last week's narrowing, and daily advance/decline plus net new highs recovered from Monday's negative prints. The tape is broad-but-momentum-light — the McClellan Summation is still at a divergent lower high, so this is a healthy bounce rather than a confirmed fresh thrust. The open questions into the 28-29 Jul FOMC: whether megacap AI earnings this week validate the semis recovery, and whether the US-Iran conflict (Brent ~$89) turns the oil tailwind for energy into a growth/inflation headwind for everything else.

flows.narrative: The freshest verifiable weekly read remained risk-on-and-stretched: BofA's Flow Show showed a historic drain of cash into risk (large money-market outflow) with global equities strongly positive, EM equities +~$25bn (strongest since Apr 2025), record-pace tech inflows (~$48.8bn over three weeks) and financials +$2.7bn. IG credit extended a 15-week inflow streak (+$9.5bn) while gold saw only a token bid. BofA's Bull & Bear Indicator sat near an extreme ~9.6 — a contrarian 'reduce risk' signal — with Mag7 capex flagged as the market's fragile last line of defense. Tuesday 21 July's tape (semis +, silver +4%, BTC five-week high) is consistent with that greedy positioning continuing to lag the CNN Fear reading (41). A fresh EPFR print was not available this run; treat these as carried figures.
